findings.description: Concatenating user-controlled url into a shell command string and calling std::system() lets an attacker inject shell metacharacters.
Concatenating user-controlled url into a shell command string and calling std::system() lets an attacker inject shell metacharacters.
Relying on PATH to resolve xdg-open, open, or am can execute a malicious binary placed earlier in PATH.
No checks on the URL’s scheme or characters; attackers could pass file:// or local paths, or control characters/newlines, etc.
start is a shell builtin with tricky quoting rules; embedding it in system introduces additional parsing ambiguities and injection risk.
Potential log injection if raw untrusted URL is logged without neutralization.
